paragraphs: Friend, here's what I think the LORD is teaching in this passage. Job has been asking God for answers, and the LORD answers with questions about lions, ravens, goats, donkeys, oxen, horses and eagles. Every one of them is fed, freed or strengthened by Him, and Job had no hand in any of it (Job 38:41; 39:5; 39:19). The point is that the One running the world is not the one who needs to be briefed on how to run it.

Then the LORD says, "Will the faultfinder contend with the Almighty? Let him who argues with God give an answer." (Job 40:2) Job replies, "Behold, I am insignificant. How can I reply to You? I place my hand over my mouth." (Job 40:4) I think that's not Job being crushed. I think that's Job finally seeing how big God is, and how small his own view of things was. I've got to tell you, friend, I spent years in a junk drawer sure I knew how my story was going to end, and I was WRONG, WRONG, WRONG.

So when your own life gets confusing, and you have a list of questions longer than a grocery receipt, you can bring them to God. But remember that He's the One who feeds the raven's young and sets the wild donkey free, and He hasn't lost track of you. Trusting Him doesn't mean you understand everything. It means you can put your hand over your mouth for a minute and let the Almighty talk. And this conversation isn't over, so stay with me.
